clue.text: Arabian money given to Italian market

parts.note: the rial is the currency of Saudi Arabia, Oman and Yemen

explanation.surface: Gulf currency is handed over to a trader in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is only a link word joining the money to TO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto in Venice is a famous historic market district by its bridge.

clue.text: Huge row from the newspaper world

definitions.meaning: an allusion to the 1986 Wapping dispute, when newspaper printers fought News International at its new Wapping plant; the answer sounds like that place name

explanation.surface: A massive quarrel breaks out in the press industry.
explanation.walkthrough: WAPPING, in east London, was where Rupert Murdoch moved his papers in 1986, setting off a bitter strike; the setter leans on the sound of that name for the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Whopping is an informal intensifier meaning remarkably large.

clue.text: If dog had his egg it was probably sick

definitions.text: If dog had his egg it was probably sick

parts.words: If dog had his egg it was probably sick
parts.note: reads as a dog (a cur) that ate someone's egg; alludes to the Punch cartoon in which a young clergyman insists his bad egg is good in parts

explanation.walkthrough: The 1895 Punch cartoon gave English the phrase 'a curate's egg', something partly good and partly bad; CUR (dog) plus ATE (had) also spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior clergyman whose famously stale breakfast egg was 'good in parts' in the cartoon.

clue.text: Dead institution, live if Irish permit revival to come in

indicators.note: the anagrammed letters come inside the word for live

parts.note: to live is to be, giving BE

indicators.note: a revival reworks something, so these letters are recast in a new order

explanation.surface: An Irish licence brings back to life a defunct organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revival' rearranges IRISH PERMIT into RITISHEMPIR, and 'to come in' puts that between B and E; 'if' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The empire ruled from London is gone, a historical institution now defunct.

clue.text: Plan about provider of hostels, possibly

indicators.note: the plan goes round the hostel body

parts.note: a map is a plan of an area
YHA is the Youth Hostels Association

explanation.surface: A scheme involving a hostel company, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The YHA, the Youth Hostels Association, runs budget hostels in England and Wales. 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning perhaps, equivalent to mayhap or perchance.

definitions.note: 12 is the police, known as the boys in blue; the answer completes that phrase

indicators.note: the letters of the next word could be made into something else by reordering

explanation.surface: Young lads might be attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 across is POLICE, the 'boys in blue'; 'could be' reworks NUBILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Policemen are nicknamed the boys in blue for their uniforms, so the phrase follows the clue words.

parts.note: people who drink heavily are said to drink like fish
to guard is to protect

explanation.surface: Boozers defend a harbour town in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: FISHGUARD is a ferry port in Pembrokeshire, west Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishguard is a Pembrokeshire harbour with ferries to Ireland.

clue.text: One wearing trousers going on jaunt is solvent

indicators.note: the one has the trousers on, so sits inside them

parts.note: pants is a word for trousers
one is the Roman numeral I
a tripper is someone going on a trip

explanation.surface: A trousered person on an outing is financially sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts I inside PANTS. 'solvent' is not about money: it is the liquid that strips paint.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical solvent sold to dissolve and remove old coats of decoration from surfaces.

clue.text: Footballer backing county student enters scolded by character in 25 down 21

parts.note: Pele, the Brazilian footballer
Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, an English county

indicators.note: the student goes into the word for scolded

parts.note: chid is an old past tense of chide, to scold
L is a learner driver's plate, a student

explanation.surface: A footballer supporting a county with a student scolded by a storybook figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' and 'enters' are the reversal and container signals. HANTS is Hampshire, a county in southern England. The definition points to Kipling's Just So Stories, the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elephant's Child is the curious hero of Kipling's tale of how the elephant got its trunk.

parts.note: an arch spans a gap
25 across is a car maker whose famous sports model is the E-type

explanation.surface: A model tool for a big cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spanner' is not a wrench but anything that spans; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is the original model or pattern of which others are copies.

clue.text: Force one to say please quickly?

indicators.note: the word is spoken rather than written
said fast, the two syllables blur into one

parts.note: the polite request word

explanation.surface: Make someone ask nicely in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: Gabbled quickly, the answer comes out sounding like 'please'; 'one' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The police are the force, as in a regional constabulary.

clue.text: Place umpire at start of play to deal with corruption

parts.note: to put is to place
ref, short for referee
... I is the first ... of a play
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: An official is posted at kick-off to tackle bribery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link. ACT I is the first act of a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Putrefaction is rotting decay, the physical sense of corruption.

clue.text: One 2 to have a problem with old servant

parts.note: one is A
2 down means huge, so big
to ail is to be unwell

explanation.surface: Someone whopping in trouble with an elderly maid.
explanation.walkthrough: An abigail is a dated word for a lady's maid, after a character in a 17th-century play.
explanation.definitionFit: Abigail was once a general term for a lady's maid, so a servant from the past.

clue.text: Saint with polygamous inhabitant could follow 11

definitions.text: Saint with polygamous inhabitant could follow 11

parts.words: Saint with polygamous inhabitant could follow 11
parts.note: a saint's name shared by a Cornish town and a Cambridgeshire one; the nursery rhyme traveller met a much-married man on his road there, and the word tacked after 11 down makes a store of records

explanation.walkthrough: The polygamist is from the rhyme 'As I was going to St ...'; joined after ARCH (11 down) the answer makes a word for a records store.
explanation.definitionFit: Several saints share the name, which is also the town in the nursery rhyme.

definitions.meaning: a drunken slurring of 'sort of', meaning more or less

explanation.surface: A tipsy speaker admits to being somewhat deficient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lesh' signals a slurred voice: 'sort of' with S slurred to SH.
explanation.definitionFit: To be short of something is to be lacking in it.

indicators.note: the blushing word holds the actress

parts.note: red, as in blushing
the Italian film star Gina Lollobrigida, given as her first name plus surname initial, the way a person might be listed

explanation.surface: A lad, blushing, hugs an Italian film star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' puts GINA L inside RED; the question mark warns that she gives first name plus initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Reginald is a boy's given name.

indicators.note: the belief goes round the people

parts.note: a tenet is a belief or doctrine
men are people

explanation.surface: A creed concerning residential accommodation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' looks like part of the wordplay (holding something) but it is the definition; 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a block of flats, a kind of housing.

definitions.meaning: a large wild cat of the Americas
8 is paint, so 'painted' in the Just So Stories

explanation.surface: A feline decorated in a storybook.
explanation.walkthrough: In Kipling's 'The Beginning of the Armadillos' the villain is called Painted Jaguar.
explanation.definitionFit: A jaguar is a big spotted cat of Central and South America.

clue.text: Nice floors give sanctified appeal to put into the good and true

definitions.note: just so means nice or precise, and floors are storeys, read cryptically as the title

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the word for the good and true

parts.note: juries are made of good men and true
ST is the abbreviation for saint
SOS is a distress appeal

explanation.surface: Neat levels lend holy pleading to an honest panel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put into' is the container signal. Juries are 'good men and true'. 'Nice floors' reads the title cryptically: just so is precise (nice), and stories is the American spelling of storeys.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice means exact, just so, and storeys are floors, making the collection's title cryptically.

clue.text: "Front her, board her, woo her, assail her" — there's something to pay, they say

definitions.text: "Front her, board her, woo her, assail her"

indicators.note: the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a cost is something to pay

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's string of advances on a woman, followed by a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is Sir Toby's definition in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost is to approach and address someone boldly, as the quotation lists.

parts.note: bras are supports
a sneck is a northern word for a door latch

explanation.surface: Ketchup holds up a latch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' means cheek or impudence, not a condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass neck is impudent nerve, the same as sauce or cheek.

definitions.meaning: ... as an adverb meaning sharply, stingingly

explanation.definitionFit: Smart can mean stinging or painful, and also neatly dressed.

definitions.meaning: having none of the five senses

explanation.surface: Unconscious and lacking all five faculties.
explanation.definitionFit: Senseless means unconscious and also lacking the physical senses.
